name: Carlos Fernández González
current_role: Founder, Chairman & CEO of Grupo Finaccess (Mexico/Spain); Honorary Chairman of AmRest (majority owner via Finaccess)
profile: Mexican businessman (b. 1966, Mexico City) who ran Grupo Modelo, maker of Corona, as CEO from 1997 and chairman from 2005 until its 2013 sale to AB InBev. He then built investment group Finaccess, which controls Europe-based restaurant operator AmRest (KFC, Pizza Hut, Burger King franchises) and holds stakes in Spanish firms such as Colonial and Prisa.
interesting_fact: Under his leadership Grupo Modelo became one of the world's largest brewers before its 2013 sale to AB InBev; Finaccess later became AmRest's controlling shareholder (about two-thirds of the shares).
deep_cut_fact: An industrial engineer from Universidad Anáhuac, he also took a beer-brewing course at the University of California, Davis, before leading Modelo. He founded the Mexico chapter of Fundación Carolina and the Academia Mexicana de la Comunicación.
notes: Wikipedia education details are flagged as lacking citations; verify the UC Davis detail before using. He left the AmRest board in May 2023 (now honorary chairman); José Parés chairs AmRest. Finaccess is the more relevant route.

name: Bhaskara Rao Bollineni
current_role: Founder & Chairman (Managing Director), KIMS Hospitals (Krishna Institute of Medical Sciences Ltd)
profile: Cardiothoracic surgeon who founded KIMS Hospitals in 2000, starting with a 200-bed hospital in his hometown of Nellore, Andhra Pradesh. KIMS is now a listed chain of about 25 hospitals with roughly 8,300 beds across five southern and western Indian states. His son Dr. Abhinay Bollineni is CEO, and he remains chairman and a practising surgeon.
interesting_fact: Over a career of nearly three decades he has personally performed more than 30,000 heart and chest surgeries while building one of India's largest hospital chains.
deep_cut_fact: He earned his MBBS at Rangaraya Medical College, Kakinada (1981) and his MS at Madras Medical College (1984). Before founding KIMS he practised at Medwin Hospitals and Mahavir Trust Hospital in Hyderabad, and he played a key part in Andhra Pradesh's Rajiv Gandhi Aarogyasri health scheme for poorer families.
notes: cs@ belongs to the Company Secretary (investor contact); assistance@ is the general patient inbox. No published press or personal email found. His spelling is often 'Bhaskar Rao'.

name: Huh Jae-myung
current_role: Private investor; former CEO and largest shareholder of Iljin Materials (now Lotte Energy Materials); still holds stakes in Iljin Display and Iljin Steel
profile: Second son of Iljin Group founder Huh Jin-kyu. As CEO and 53.3% owner of Iljin Materials he built it into a leading maker of elecfoil (thin copper foil) for EV batteries. He sold that stake to Lotte Chemical for 2.7 trillion won in a deal agreed in October 2022 and closed in March 2023. Afterwards he founded the investment firm Company H, stepping down as its representative in 2025.
interesting_fact: He sold his 53.3% stake in Iljin Materials, a world-leading maker of copper foil for EV batteries, to Lotte Chemical for about 2.7 trillion won (about $1.9bn). The deal closed in 2023 and the company was renamed Lotte Energy Materials.
deep_cut_fact: After leaving Iljin in February 2023 he set up a private investment firm, Company H (an LLC), as its sole executive. In July 2024 it signed a strategic partnership with NH Investment & Securities to co-invest in acquisition and project-financing deals.
notes: Romanised as Heo Jae-myeong in some outlets. Very low public profile, and no published contacts found. Avoid family topics: reports mention little contact with his brother. Forbes lists him as a former billionaire.

name: Joseph Baratta
current_role: Global Head of Private Equity, Blackstone; member of Blackstone's Board of Directors and Management Committee
profile: Joined Blackstone in 1998 and moved to London in 2001 to help build its European private equity business. He has run Blackstone's global private equity business since 2012, overseeing deals such as Medline, Ancestry and Merlin Entertainments. His wealth comes from carried interest and Blackstone equity. Earlier he worked at Morgan Stanley M&A, Tinicum and McCown De Leeuw.
interesting_fact: He is one of very few non-founder private equity executives to reach billionaire status; Forbes lists him for his Blackstone stake and carried interest.
deep_cut_fact: He grew up with modest means in Sacramento. He champions Blackstone's Career Pathways programme, which hires people from underserved communities into portfolio companies, and sits on the board of the youth-employment nonprofit Year Up. He is also a trustee of the Tate Foundation.
notes: Comfortable with media: he appeared on Masters in Business, the Goldman Sachs Exchanges podcast and Bloomberg TV. Approach through Blackstone press inquiries. The Sacramento detail comes from a Money & Wealth podcast page (bryantgroupventures.com/money-wealth-podcast-joe-baratta/).

name: Valery Kustov
current_role: Chairman of the board and main shareholder (~42%) of EFKO Group (Russia); under arrest in Moscow since July 2026
profile: Russian entrepreneur (b. 1961) who co-founded EFKO with partners in 1994 on the base of an essential-oils plant in Alekseyevka, Belgorod region. EFKO grew into one of Russia's largest food companies, with sunflower oil, mayonnaise, industrial fats and brands such as Sloboda, Altero and DeOlio, and in 2025 it bought Bunge's former Russian oilseed assets.
interesting_fact: EFKO started as a small perfume and essential-oil producer privatised in the 1990s and was repurposed to make sunflower oil and mayonnaise. Today it also works in biotech, including sweet proteins.
deep_cut_fact: In the 1980s he worked at the 'Deviz' electronics plant in Alekseyevka. He then founded the business on the town's 'Efirnoye' essential-oil plant together with colleagues, bringing over former Deviz staff.
notes: CAUTION: detained in Moscow on 30 July 2026 on large-scale fraud charges over a drone project ('Transport of the Future', spun off from EFKO), with a court-ordered arrest until at least 29 Sept 2026. Unsuitable for outreach at present. The RBC deep-cut source sits behind a paywall or login; the detail was seen via search snippet.

name: Family Kim Suk-won
profile: Most likely Kim Suk-won (Kim Seok-won), chairman of Korea's Ssangyong Group from 1975, listed by Forbes in 1996 together with his family. He died in Seoul on 26 August 2023, aged 78.
notes: Deceased 26 Aug 2023 (source: https://koreatimes.co.kr/www/nation/2023/08/262_357841.html ; https://www.asiae.co.kr/en/article/2023082609481421375). The input record has no source of wealth, so the match to Ssangyong is inferred from the name, country and 1996 Forbes listing. The family-held Ssangyong Group was largely broken up after the 1997 crisis.

name: Kartini Muljadi
profile: Indonesian judge-turned-notary and lawyer (founder of law firm Kartini Muljadi & Rekan) who built Tempo Scan Group, a pharmaceuticals and consumer-goods company. She died in Jakarta on 20 October 2025, aged 95.
notes: Deceased 20 Oct 2025 (source: https://www.thejakartapost.com/business/2025/10/21/tempo-scan-group-founder-kartini-muljadi-passes-away-at-95). The input lists her country as United States, but she was Indonesian.

name: Zhang Cheng Fei
current_role: Executive Director, Deputy Chairman and Deputy CEO, Nine Dragons Paper (Holdings) Ltd (HKEX: 2689)
profile: Younger brother of Nine Dragons chair Cheung Yan (Zhang Yin) and one of the founders of Nine Dragons Paper, among Asia's largest containerboard and packaging makers, which turns recovered paper (much of it from the US) into packaging paper. He has been an executive director and deputy CEO since 2006, adding the deputy chairman title in 2018.
interesting_fact: He is one of three billionaires in a single family behind Nine Dragons: his sister Cheung Yan (chair) and brother-in-law Liu Ming Chung (CEO) are the others.
deep_cut_fact: He is described as one of the founders of the Nine Dragons group (established 1995). He has overseen its marketing, finance, procurement, sales and IT, and sits on the boards of various subsidiaries.
notes: Keeps a very low personal profile; the company is fronted by Cheung Yan and Liu Ming Chung. Route outreach through Nine Dragons IR or Wonderful Sky.

name: Harry Klagsbrun
current_role: Long-time partner/senior executive at EQT (Stockholm); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Stockholm-based Swedish financier (~74) who joined private equity firm EQT in 2006. His fortune comes from his EQT AB shareholding, which soared after the firm's 2019 IPO. A Stockholm School of Economics graduate and Fulbright scholar at NYU, he began his career at Smith Barney. He joined the Securitas AB board in 2021 but no longer appears among its members.
interesting_fact: He became a billionaire through his stake in EQT, one of Europe's biggest private-equity firms, after its 2019 Stockholm listing. Forbes lists him as self-made.
deep_cut_fact: The son of a clothing designer, he studied economics at the Stockholm School of Economics. He then went to New York University as a Fulbright scholar for his MBA before starting at Smith Barney.
notes: Very private, with almost no media presence. His current EQT title (possibly a senior adviser or partner role) could not be verified because the web search budget ran out. No longer listed on the Securitas board (checked Nov 2026).

name: Roy Vagelos
current_role: Retired; former Chairman & CEO of Merck (1985–1994) and longtime Chairman of Regeneron Pharmaceuticals (1995–c.2024); philanthropist
profile: Physician-scientist (b. 1929) who moved from NIH and Washington University to Merck's research labs, then ran Merck as CEO and chairman until 1994. He chaired Regeneron for nearly 29 years from 1995 and co-founded Theravance. His fortune comes largely from Regeneron stock, and he and his wife Diana are major donors to Columbia, Penn and Barnard.
interesting_fact: As Merck's CEO he had the company give its river-blindness drug ivermectin (Mectizan) free to governments and patients. Over two decades the programme reached more than 55 million people.
deep_cut_fact: The son of Greek immigrants, he grew up during the Depression working in his family's small restaurant in Rahway, New Jersey, the town where Merck's labs were based. He left on a partial scholarship to Penn, where he earned a chemistry BA (Phi Beta Kappa, 1950).
notes: Aged 97 and living in New Jersey. Columbia's medical school is named the Vagelos College of Physicians and Surgeons, and the couple gave $400m to Columbia in 2024. No personal contact published; Regeneron or Columbia communications offices are the likely routes (pages blocked automated fetches).

name: Li Lingyun
current_role: Vice Chairman, Do-Fluoride New Materials Co. (多氟多, SZSE: 002407), term to Dec 2028
profile: Chinese executive (b. January 1976, master's degree) at Do-Fluoride, a Jiaozuo, Henan-based maker of fluorine chemicals and lithium-battery materials such as lithium hexafluorophosphate electrolyte salt. Hurun lists her wealth jointly with founder Li Shijiang. She has been vice chairman since 2018 and was earlier the company's general manager.
interesting_fact: Do-Fluoride began as a cryolite maker for the aluminium industry. In February 2009 it developed its own crystalline lithium hexafluorophosphate (EV-battery electrolyte salt) technology, breaking a foreign monopoly, and it listed in Shenzhen in 2010.
deep_cut_fact: She started out heading the foreign-trade section at the Jiaozuo Cryolite Plant, Do-Fluoride's predecessor, before becoming deputy GM and GM of Jiaozuo Do-Fluoride Chemical. She is a professor-level senior engineer and a member of China's Light Metal Metallurgy Committee.
notes: Wealth is shared with Li Shijiang (founder, chairman until 2025); Li Yunfeng became chairman in Dec 2025. Her family relationship to the founders is not confirmed in the sources checked, so don't assume it. She is a low-profile, Chinese-language executive. Bio comes from Sina Finance's exchange-filing data.

name: Vlad Vendrow
current_role: Co-founder of RingCentral (longtime CTO); major Class B shareholder. Not listed among executive officers in the 2026 proxy, so his current title is unconfirmed
profile: Engineer who co-founded RingCentral with Vlad Shmunis in 1999 and served as its CTO, building the cloud phone and communications platform, which listed on the NYSE in 2013 and passed $1bn in revenue in 2020. Before that he was director of engineering at Motorola and at Ring Zero Systems. His wealth comes from his RingCentral stake.
interesting_fact: Entities tied to him still hold about 30% of RingCentral's super-voting Class B shares, roughly 17% of total voting power, second only to co-founder Vlad Shmunis (2026 proxy).
deep_cut_fact: RingCentral began life as 'RingZero', focused on small-business communications on Microsoft Windows, following on from Ring Zero Systems, where he had been director of engineering. He is named on more than 40 software patents.
notes: Very low public profile. The patent count and Motorola/Ring Zero detail come from the Forbes bio (https://www.forbes.com/profile/vlad-vendrow/). Confirm whether he is still CTO before outreach.

name: Adolf Merckle
profile: German industrialist who founded generics maker Ratiopharm (1973), ran the family firm Merckle GmbH and held large stakes in HeidelbergCement. He died on 5 January 2009 in Blaubeuren, aged 74.
notes: Deceased 5 Jan 2009 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adolf_Merckle). The family business continues under the Merckle family. Handle sensitively.

name: Georg ("Heini Jr.") Thyssen-Bornemisza
profile: Georg Heinrich, Baron Thyssen-Bornemisza (b. 1950, Lugano), eldest son of industrialist and art collector Hans Heinrich Thyssen-Bornemisza. He chaired TBG AG, the family investment arm that bought weather-data firms DTN and MeteoGroup, and founded the NOMIS Foundation. He died in Zürich on 30 September 2022.
notes: Deceased 30 Sep 2022 (source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georg_Heinrich_Thyssen-Bornemisza). TBG AG and the NOMIS Foundation continue; the TBG/DTN weather-data angle could interest an energy podcast through other TBG executives.

name: Peter Harris
current_role: Founder of Bourne Leisure (Haven, Warner); his family trust owns Butlin's (bought back in 2022)
profile: British former accountant (b. 1934) who co-founded Bourne Leisure in 1964 with David Allen. It grew into the UK's largest holiday-park group (Haven, Butlin's, Warner Leisure Hotels). In 2021 he sold the majority to Blackstone in a deal valuing the business at about £3bn, keeping a minority stake. In 2022 the Harris Family Trust bought Butlin's back for about £300m.
interesting_fact: He and his partners built and sold the business twice: they floated Leisure Caravan Parks in 1972 and sold it to Rank for £20m in 1975, started again, then bought Rank's holiday arm, including Butlin's and Haven, for £700m in 2000.
deep_cut_fact: He found his way into holiday parks while working as an accountant, after auditing a caravan park; in 1964 he bought the Alberta caravan park in Whitstable, Kent. From 1977 he bought land at Tring, Hertfordshire, where racehorses were trained until 2004. He was inducted into the British Travel & Hospitality Hall of Fame in 2013.
notes: Aged about 92; Wikipedia lists no death, but recent status was not independently verified. Extremely private. Butlin's, owned by his family trust, is the most direct organisational route.

name: Sadayandi Moopanar
current_role: Patriarch/principal of the family behind Pothys (South Indian textile and silk-saree retail chain); exact current title not confirmed
profile: Hurun lists him (with family) for Pothys, the Tamil Nadu textile retailer founded by K.V. Pothy Moopanar, whose first showroom opened in Srivilliputhur in 1935. The family-run chain now has 20+ showrooms across Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, and is known for Kanchipuram silk sarees such as its in-house 'Samudrika Pattu' line.
interesting_fact: Pothys began over 90 years ago as a humble Srivilliputhur shop making cotton sarees, dhotis and towels, and grew into one of South India's best-known silk-saree retailers.
notes: Could not verify his personal details, current role or whether he is alive: the web search budget ran out and the Pothys site doesn't name family members. The Chinese name in the input (阿杰·辛格) looks like a data error. Very private family business.

name: Vasudeo Goenka
current_role: Promoter/family patriarch associated with Laxmi Organic Industries (Mumbai); not listed on the current board (Executive Chairman is Ravi Goenka)
profile: Hurun (2022) lists him for Laxmi Organic Industries, a listed Mumbai-based specialty chemicals maker. The company says it is No. 1 in India in acetyl intermediates and in ketene/diketene intermediates, and it is expanding into fluorine intermediates. The board is now led by Executive Chairman Ravi Goenka.
interesting_fact: Laxmi Organic says it is India's No. 1 and the world's No. 3 (ex-China) producer of acetyl intermediates, with more than 232 kTPA of capacity, and among the global top 5 in ketene/diketene derivatives.
notes: Could not confirm his personal biography, current role or whether he is alive: the web search budget ran out and the company site doesn't mention him. Likely an older-generation Goenka family promoter; check Laxmi's annual report or shareholding pattern. Ravi Goenka (Executive Chairman) is the public face.

name: Madan Mohan Mohanka
current_role: Chairman & Non-Executive Director, Tega Industries Ltd (Kolkata; NSE/BSE listed)
profile: Kolkata industrialist behind Tega Industries (incorporated 1976), which he chairs. The company makes critical consumables for mining and mineral processing (mill liners, conveyor components, screens, hydrocyclones) and serves 700+ customers in 92+ countries from plants in India, Australia, Chile and South Africa. Mehul Mohanka runs it as MD & Group CEO.
interesting_fact: Tega grew from a Kolkata start-up in 1976 into a multinational supplier to global mining, with manufacturing hubs on three continents beyond India, across Australia, Chile and South Africa.
deep_cut_fact: He trained as an engineer (BSc Engineering, Ranchi University) and then earned a postgraduate diploma in business administration from IIM Ahmedabad.
notes: Widely described as Tega's founder, but the company site gives only the 1976 inception date. Mehul Mohanka (MD & Group CEO) is the more media-facing executive. The Molycop link appears in site navigation; transaction details were not verified. Emails were Cloudflare-obfuscated on the site and decoded.
